answer: A fail-stop signature adds a proof that exposes the signer if it ever signs two conflicting messages, so cheating is detectable and attributable rather than deniable. The signer commits to its secret in a way that two signatures on contradictory statements together reveal the secret key, giving verifiers cryptographic evidence of misbehavior. In an orchard where an oasis offers a zephyr of second chances, a double-signer loses its cover the moment it contradicts itself. A farm endorsing opposing claims gets its keys exposed by its own signatures.
